evp.title: Our Banking Client: shared QA platform
evp.lead: A payment-release story: 75 offshore QA staff, heavy manual testing and constrained test environments.
evp.note: Executive briefing • Strategic vision • Client scenario

evp.title: The QA organization
evp.lead: 75 offshore QA staff across five squads; 45 focus on manual and domain testing. Environments and vendor test slots limit parallel work.
evp.note: The pilot draws eight QA staff from this population. More engineers alone do not create more vendor test capacity.

evp.title: QE testing scenario: one timeout, two debits
evp.lead: PAY-142 simulates a CAD 100 transfer accepted before a timeout. The customer retries; an injected duplicate-posting defect tests whether QE catches the second debit.
evp.note: Expected: one transfer, one balanced journal and one customer-visible result. This is a QE test scenario, not a reported client incident.

evp.title: Where the release work goes
evp.lead: Modelled hands-on effort for one bounded release test pack. Eight stages add to 300 hours.
evp.note: The pack spans 10 business days. Waiting time and human effort use different units and must be measured separately.

evp.title: The platform investment
evp.lead: Common context, fixtures and evidence serve every squad. Application teams retain business ownership.
evp.note: Existing test frameworks and pipelines execute approved work. AI supports preparation and interpretation.

evp.title: Before / after: separate modernization from AI
evp.note: Same payment scope. The two target states are proposed; no productivity or quality improvement has been measured.

evp.title: Delivery maturity changes the first move
evp.lead: The same tool creates different work in a shared manual environment and a repeatable delivery system.
evp.note: These profiles illustrate effort, not adoption approval. Review twelve dependency areas before committing to scope, dates or benefits.

evp.title: What 78 hours of gross capacity means
evp.lead: Mixed-maturity target: 300 hours becomes 222, including 40 hours of review.
evp.note: Conditional capacity arithmetic; adoption prerequisites are unverified. Tool, cloud and vendor charges are excluded. This is not cash ROI or measured AI impact.

evp.title: Ownership within the offshore model
rows: Shared enablement
Own context adapters, templates, fixtures, runner integration and coaching.
Application QA teams
Own business scenarios, expected results, execution and defect disposition.
Product and release owners
Resolve requirement questions and accept the release evidence.
Delivery management
Provide repository access, overlap hours and an explicit backlog for freed capacity.
evp.note: Reskill domain testers through paired reviews. Agree supplier incentives and reuse ownership before scaling.

evp.title: Observed time framework for the API pilot
evp.lead: Record actual pilot time from baseline through repeated API runs. Example windows remain subject to readiness.
evp.note: Planning windows are illustrative. Environment, data, virtualization and reviewer readiness determine when each phase can progress.

evp.title: The evidence needed to expand
rows: Quality
All mandatory payment assertions pass; no unexplained skips or weakened checks.
Effort
Include preparation, review, correction, retesting and platform operation.
Delivery
Report elapsed time, waiting reasons and failed-run recovery separately.
Reuse
A second squad runs the pattern and maintains it without the pilot authors.
evp.note: A faster draft is insufficient. Compare tasks of similar scope and retain conventional work as a reference.

evp.title: Brainstorm questions
evp.lead: The next decision: assess one payment workflow with QA, development and platform leads.
points: “Across the 75 QA staff, where do people spend time and where are they waiting?”
“Which payment journey has stable requirements, observable outcomes and an owner who can join a pilot?”
“Could one platform team remove duplicated work across the squads?”
“If we return capacity, which backlog or release commitment will use it?”
evp.note: Agree the bounded pilot and its evidence before promising wider rollout. See the discovery brief for owners, commercial scope and timing.

evp.title: Adoption depends on funded foundations
evp.note: Our Banking Client has not been assessed. The dependency backlog can change scope, cost and timing; the 480-hour setup allowance is not a client quote.

evp.title: Modernization enables wider AI adoption
evp.note: For Our Banking Client, fund repeatable payment tests and shared QE services alongside reviewed AI assistance. Validate this capability roadmap through client discovery.

evp.title: Peer evidence for the payments pilot
evp.note: Peer results support a trial. Outcomes for Our Banking Client remain unmeasured.

evp.title: Our Banking Client: where to begin
evp.note: Choose one entry point, validate its prerequisites and agree how reviewers will judge the result. Wider rollout depends on local evidence.

evp.title: Four layers of AI-assisted QE
evp.note: Authored roadmap. Expand with validated prerequisites and client evidence.

evp.title: Before / after: the shared QE architecture
evp.note: Starting point: heavy manual QE and scarce vendor environments. Pilot target: controlled service tests, with real integration still required.

evp.title: Outcomes beyond hours
evp.note: Business aims: fewer escaped payment defects and emergency fixes. These proposed pilot measures do not establish those outcomes.

evp.title: What AI contributes, from requirement to release
evp.note: PAY-142 is an authored scenario. Each AI output needs review; test runners execute and people decide.

evp.title: Follow one payment test through the handoffs
evp.note: Illustrative artifacts and outcomes. Preserve failed evidence; a passing retest alone does not approve release.

technical.title: Our Banking Client: engineering blueprint
technical.lead: Follow one payment test from an approved contract to isolated execution and inspectable evidence.
technical.note: Technical design review · Authored reference architecture; validate interfaces and tooling with the client.

technical.title: The application landscape
technical.lead: Payment APIs offer the first controlled test surface. Other applications follow their own readiness.
technical.note: Current baseline: few shared environments and no backend virtualization. WireMock and per-run isolation are proposed pilot capabilities.

technical.title: Separate authoring from test execution
technical.note: Adapters and joined evidence are integration work to build. Model output cannot change the original assertion result.

technical.title: PAY-142: request contract and test oracle
technical.note: Authored contract; minor units are CAD cents. Start at 100000 / 0; no fees, FX or other account activity.

technical.title: Timeout and retry: the runtime sequence
technical.note: QE testing scenario. A timeout leaves the outcome unknown; a stable key must resolve to the original transfer.

technical.title: Version the context before asking for a test
technical.note: Proposed artifacts for the client scenario; identifiers and conflict behavior require agreement with the API owner.

technical.title: Pin and reset the test environment
technical.note: Proposed manifest schema. Digest and commit placeholders must resolve to real immutable versions before execution.

technical.title: Assert money movement, not just HTTP status
technical.note: Non-runnable pseudocode for this CAD 100 test scenario; a REST Assured/JUnit implementation needs approved API and ledger helpers.

technical.title: The appropriate test layer
rows: Developer unit
Copilot drafts JUnit tests for idempotency logic; developers review. A fake repository cannot prove real payment integration.
Service and API
REST Assured + JUnit. Cover retry, concurrent requests, idempotency conflicts and journal outcomes.
Web journey
Playwright for the new React flow. Check pending state, retry action and the final customer message.
Existing browser and mobile
Keep owned Selenium and Appium coverage. Change frameworks only when maintenance evidence supports it.
Batch and integration
Retain settlement-file reconciliation and provider sandbox checks with explicit scheduling.
technical.note: Test distribution follows behavior and observability. A new browser framework does not solve a shared settlement environment.

technical.title: Publish raw CI results before AI interpretation
technical.note: Microsoft task syntax is documented; the AI adapter is proposed integration work. Job cancellation can still prevent artifact collection.

technical.title: Route failures without rewriting the verdict
technical.note: Proposed diagnostic schema and routing policy. Human review assigns the disposition; the original evidence remains available.

technical.title: Define the run evidence contract
technical.note: Proposed evidence contract and pilot gate. This example does not supply a complete banking release policy.

technical.title: Challenge the test with failure injection
rows: Duplicate journal defect
Second posting changes payer to 80000; journal / balance checks fail.
Same key, changed amount
Conflict returned; no additional provider submission or journal.
Concurrent same-key retries
One transfer identity and one journal after all attempts settle.
Repeated callback event
Same event ID produces no additional posting.
technical.note: Author the expected behavior independently. The browser demo covers a subset; these cases require service-level implementation.

technical.title: Readiness requires executable proof
rows: Deploy + reset
Pinned application digest starts; a fresh run restores the same synthetic balances.
Provider control
Replay timeout and duplicate callback; identify the model revision and its owner.
Observable outcome
Read transfer identity and committed journal facts without depending on the AI summary.
Reproduction
A second engineer reruns the same manifest and obtains an explainable outcome.
technical.note: Assess per application. Unknown or failed checks block the dependent execution scope; reviewed drafting has a narrower prerequisite set.

technical.title: Offshore handoff and platform ownership
technical.lead: Each handoff carries a reproducible artifact and a named next owner.
technical.note: Pilot team: one QA lead, four domain testers, two automation engineers and one data/environment engineer. Product, development and platform support contribute separately.

technical.title: Correlate a failure across the runtime
technical.note: Proposed observability contract. Example identifiers are illustrative; the AI hypothesis does not override the failed assertion.

technical.title: Promotion rules for a generated test
rows: Code + intent review
Approved behavior and independent assertions; no weakened checks or unexplained skips.
Paired challenge
Correct build passes; injected duplicate posting fails using identical fixtures.
Reproducibility
Run manifest, raw evidence and cleanup results are present; repeat failures are classified.
Suite promotion
QA owner approves the PR; required tests and separate integration checks remain enforced.
technical.note: Do not promote a generated test merely because it compiles or passes once. Benchmark pilot effort separately.

technical.title: Brainstorm questions: API architecture
points: Where is idempotency enforced: API, provider request, journal transaction and callback handler?
Which artifact proves one posting when the response is lost or the callback is duplicated?
Can two engineers reproduce the same failure from a pinned manifest and fresh fixtures?
Who owns provider-model drift, failed cleanup and evidence retention?
technical.note: Resolve the contract, repeatability, ownership and evidence questions with system owners before expanding execution authority.

technical.title: Map foundation gaps to blocked capabilities
rows: Approved rules + repository context
Reviewed test drafting; without a trustworthy oracle, keep cases as unapproved proposals.
Isolated runner + resettable fixtures
Automated service execution; shared mutable data prevents repeatable comparisons.
Provider models + contract owner
Deterministic negative-path tests; unknown model fidelity needs real integration evidence.
Run IDs + raw results + named owner
Evidence-linked diagnosis and team reuse; missing evidence routes to investigation.
technical.note: Foundation work starts with the pilot. Existing DevOps and QE maturity determine which capability can progress.

technical.title: Service virtualization and real integration
technical.lead: Control the payment provider for repeatable tests; keep a separate real-integration gate.
technical.note: WireMock is an HTTP example. Contract fidelity, callback behavior and batch access need explicit owners; passing a stub does not prove end-to-end correctness.

technical.title: Our Banking Client: test environment
technical.note: The CI runner checks the real payment service and database against reviewed provider models. Retain separate provider and settlement evidence.

technical.title: Technology roles in the payment pilot
technical.note: Choose Testcontainers, Compose or an existing supported environment for the test scope. Mobile devices and legacy settlement retain their own integration requirements.

technical.title: A candidate test must earn acceptance
technical.note: PAY-142 must catch an incorrect transfer, journal or balance. The guided example rejects the candidate and leaves the maintained suite unchanged.

technical.title: Instrument the pilot at run level
technical.note: Authored measurement schema; no pilot timing, cost or effectiveness observations have been recorded.

technical.title: The runtime from setup to cleanup
technical.note: Repeatable execution is a platform capability. Retain failure evidence and attempt cleanup on every path; real integration remains separate.

technical.title: Integration adapters have explicit contracts
technical.lead: Reuse CI execution and artifact storage. Add owned context, model and evidence adapters around those systems.
rows: Context / QE platform
Story + API + test revisions → bundle; unresolved rules block approval of affected cases.
Model / AI platform
Bundle + configuration → patch; timeout or quota → no candidate, bounded retry.
Runner / application QA
Approved test commit + manifest → raw results; preserve exit status, retain evidence, clean up.
Evidence / QE platform
Run artifacts → indexed links; incomplete joins stay unknown; AI report is read-only.
technical.note: Proposed adapter contracts. Use request IDs for safe retries and record attempts; platform owners define timeouts and retention.

technical.title: Before / after: the API test architecture
technical.note: 75 offshore QA staff share constrained environments. Proposed isolation and virtualized dependencies support parallel service tests; real integration stays scheduled.
technical.chapter: Before and after the API pilot

technical.title: How the four AI adoption layers connect
technical.note: Proposed integration paths. The CI assistant is read-only; bounded agents need isolated tools, independent checks and human approval.

technical.title: Measure test effectiveness and decision evidence
technical.note: A clean control must pass; the intended injected-fault assertion must fail. Coverage and complete evidence do not imply a release pass.

technical.title: Prove reliability, integration and reuse
technical.note: A passing retry never erases failure. Stubs do not prove real integration. Agree the independence of the reuse trial before measuring.

technical.title: Nine AI-assisted steps, with explicit handoffs
technical.note: AI drafts; reviewers approve; CI executes. Context, artifacts and evidence remain versioned.

technical.title: PAY-142: requirement, test, failure, fix and proof
technical.note: Authored trace IDs. Fixed assertions: original transfer ID, one journal, payer 90000 and recipient 10000 minor units.

technical.title: Three states: isolate the incremental AI contribution
technical.note: Compare equivalent payment packs. Retain real-provider checks and measure review, rework and platform overhead.
